description_en: The temple is located within the religious complex of Dhuleśvara, on a hill 3,5 km north of Dullu.The site of Dhuleśvara is part of an area know as Pañcakośī. The sites of the Pañcakośī are visited by pilgrims from all over western Nepal. The sites are notorious for their flame temples (natural gas flames), said to mark places where Satī's body parts fell while Śiva carried her charred body (Lecomte-Tilouine 2009). While parts like the Satī's head (sirā) fell in Sīrasthān (DLK0130), the rest of the body, reduced to dust (dhūli), fell in Dhuleśvara.The monument has two stories. A veranda opens on the south. To the east and north are two doors. Along the eastern facade is a flight of stairs leading to the upper storey. The ground floor is divided in three rooms, a kitchen (in the veranda space), a room containing thedhunifire with where the temple'smahantperforms rituals and room with beds for the priests in charge of the Jvālā Ghar (DLK0331).According to local informants the monument was built in 1943 CE (1999 VS).
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)
references: REFERENCES Lecomte-Tilouine, Marie. 2009, “The Panchakoshi of Dullu. The Fire Frame of the Malla Imperial Capital”, in Bards and Mediums. History, Culture and Politics in the Central Himalayan Kingdoms , Marie Lecomte-Tilouine (ed.). Almora: Almora Book Depot, pp. 253-276.
